name: BILLITONNEN
description: Billitonnen is a traditional Dutch domino game belonging to the 'Blind Hughie' family. Players draw their tiles but keep them face-down in a row, turning them over one at a time to play. The strong element of luck is tempered by memory—if you can remember the positions of tiles you've seen others fail to play, you gain a significant advantage. Traditionally played as light relief after a session of the more serious Dutch game Nos.

content.text: Billitonnen is a traditional Dutch domino game belonging to the 'Blind Hughie' family. Players draw their tiles but keep them face-down in a row, turning them over one at a time to play. The strong element of luck is tempered by memory—if you can remember the positions of tiles you've seen others fail to play, you gain a significant advantage. Traditionally played as light relief after a session of the more serious Dutch game Nos.

Originating in the Netherlands, Billitonnen takes its name from Billiton (Belitung), an Indonesian island formerly part of the Dutch East Indies. It is a lighthearted variant of European line games, prized for its chaotic and social nature.
Players draw tiles based on count (2p=7, 3p=7, 4p=6). Tiles are placed in a face-down row in front of each player. No one may look at their tiles.

items.text: Blind Hughie: The English variant where players may sometimes choose which tile to flip instead of the leftmost.
